sections.body: Cheerful resin decor for children's tanks and classroom aquariums. It is non-toxic, weighted and paint-sealed, so it sits on the substrate and the colour stays on.

Rinse it in clean water and look it over for sharp edges or chips that could snag a fin. Leave plenty of open swimming space around it, and take it out and clean it with a soft brush if algae builds up. If paint starts to flake, remove it from the tank.

A submersible heater with a digital display and built-in thermostat readout, for tropical tanks and turtle setups. You can see the set temperature at a glance, which takes the guesswork out of a dial.

As a rule of thumb a heater of roughly half a watt to one watt per litre handles most rooms, with more for a cold room. Check the wattage on the product you choose against your tank volume, and use the [tank-size pages](/tanks) for examples. Place it near the filter outflow, where flow spreads the heat, and keep it clear of plants and decor. With turtles, use a heater guard, because turtles can bump and break an unprotected heater.

Let the heater sit in the water for a few minutes before turning it on, and unplug it and let it cool before taking it out, for example during a water change. Check the temperature with a separate [thermometer](/product/digital-thermometer-lcd), so you are not relying on one device.
Thirty-eight pounds of polished mixed river rock, enough to scope a 4-foot tank and to rescape later. Smooth stone suits a natural riverbed look, a stream border or a base layer around larger rocks.

Check whether the rock changes your water. Put a few drops of vinegar on a sample. If it fizzes, the rock contains carbonate and will raise hardness and pH over time, which suits African cichlids but not soft-water shrimp or most planted tanks. No fizz means it is likely to be inert. Test your water's hardness a week after adding the rock.

Wash the rocks in a bucket with clean water until it runs clear. Do not use soap. Place larger stones on the glass base or on a plate of slate first so that digging fish cannot undermine them and cause a collapse. Use with [aqua soil](/product/aqua-soil-planted-substrate) around the edges for a planted look.

Feed pellets and powders into one spot rather than scattering them across the tank. The tube guides food down into a glass dish, which holds it above the substrate so shrimp eat it all. Nothing rots in the soil overnight.

Buried pellets foul a planted tank and are a common cause of problems with pests such as planaria. A dish makes it easy to see how much has been eaten and to remove what is left after a few hours. It also draws the colony into view, so you can count them and spot berried females. Pair it with [shrimp tablets](/product/blizzard-shrimp-tablets-spinach) and feed small amounts.

A modular mesh grid that divides a tank for fry, for a bullying fish, as a hospital bay or to keep two males apart. Cut it to size, clip pieces together and rearrange it as often as you like. It comes in 30 x 15 cm half-sheets and 30 x 30 cm full sheets, which can be combined to fit a standard tank width.

sections.h: Why a grid and not a solid divider
sections.body: Water flows through the open grid, so filtration and heat are shared across both sides and no second filter is needed. Fish can see each other, which keeps some aggressive fish calmer than a solid wall. Check the gap size against your smallest fish, as tiny fry can slip through wide grids, and use a [breeder box](/product/acrylic-breeder-box-hang-on) for newborns.
Cut with scissors or a sharp knife, and file any rough edges. Wedge the divider tightly against the glass and the substrate, so that fish cannot push under it, and cover the top if your fish jump.

sections.h: A staple flake for community tanks
sections.body: An everyday flake for guppies, tetras, barbs, danios and other fish that feed near the top. It is soft enough for small mouths to crush and made not to cloud the water. The formula includes spirulina and shrimp meal for steady colour.

Feed only what the fish eat in a minute or two, once or twice a day, and skip a day each week. Flakes float first, then drift down for mid-water fish, so watch where the food goes. Leftovers foul the water and cause algae. Vary the diet with [bloodworm cubes](/product/freeze-dried-bloodworm-cubes) a few times a week.
Close the tub tightly after each use and keep it cool and dry. Flake loses vitamins over time, so use it within a few months of opening rather than buying the biggest tub.

Micro pellets sized for a betta's upturned mouth, with a high-protein, fish-meal-first formula suited to an insectivore's gut. Natural colour enhancers help keep reds and blues deep. A small spoon is included to help you avoid overfeeding.

Overfeeding is the most common cause of betta problems. Give two to four pellets once or twice a day, depending on the size of the fish, and remove anything left after a few minutes. A betta's stomach is about the size of its eye. Fast the fish for a day each week.

Bettas do well with a mixed diet, so add an occasional treat of [freeze-dried bloodworm](/product/freeze-dried-bloodworm-cubes). Combine it with a calm tank, a [leaf hammock](/product/betta-leaf-hammock) and warm water.

Fancy goldfish such as ranchu, oranda, lionhead and ryukin have round bodies, and gulping air at the surface can cause swim-bladder problems. These soft sinking pellets drop to the fish instead of making them surface-feed. They are spirulina-enriched for colour and digestion.

Goldfish are grazers that produce a lot of waste, so feed small amounts a few times a day, and soak the pellets for a minute before feeding if the fish tend to bloat. A pellet formula for growth suits young fish, and adults do not need as much protein. Pair with vegetables such as blanched peas or spinach.

Goldfish tanks need strong filtration and regular water changes. Check ammonia and nitrite with [test strips](/product/test-strips-8-in-1-100-count) and change water weekly. Uneaten pellets break down quickly, so siphon any that are left.

Dense sinking wafers that hold together long enough for night-active fish, such as plecos, bristlenose, corydoras and larger catfish, to find them. They stay intact for the first hour rather than dissolving into mush that ends up in the filter. The formula balances algae and protein, because pure algae is not a complete diet.

Drop a wafer in shortly before the lights go out, so that the nocturnal fish find it when they come out. Feed one wafer per fish or group, and remove any remaining pieces in the morning. If other fish steal the wafer, feed it in a spot where bottom feeders can reach it first.
Plecos and some catfish rasp wood as part of their diet, so provide some [driftwood](/product/natural-driftwood-branch) alongside wafers.
Freeze-dried tubifex worm cubes give a denser protein hit than bloodworms and are a favourite for conditioning breeding pairs. A cube sticks to wet glass, so the whole tank can feed in view.

Wet a cube, press it to the glass below the waterline and let fish pick at it. Use it a couple of times a week as a treat, not a daily staple. Variety matters, so alternate with [bloodworm](/product/freeze-dried-bloodworm-cubes) and a quality flake or pellet. Remove any remains after a few minutes to keep the water clean.
Keep the tub sealed and dry. Freeze-dried food absorbs moisture from the air, which spoils it, so avoid opening it over the tank where steam rises.

A clear acrylic feeding station that suctions to the inside of the glass. Flakes and pellets go in the top chute, and fish learn to feed in one spot. Food stops drifting into the filter or landing under rocks.

A fixed feeding point makes it easy to see how much is eaten, and it keeps uneaten food from fouling the substrate. It also helps fish that are shy of the surface, because a station gives them a routine. Place it away from the filter outflow so that food does not get blown out.

It works best with flakes and small pellets. Clean the station with a soft brush and rinse it with clean water when algae film builds up. Pair with a quality flake such as [tropical flakes](/product/tropical-fish-flakes-100g).

sections.h: Pick the wattage by tank volume
sections.body: The heater comes in five sizes: 25 W for 20 to 40 litre tanks, 50 W for 40 to 80 L, 100 W for 80 to 150 L, 200 W for 150 to 250 L and 300 W for 250 to 400 L. Count the water volume, not the label size, since substrate and hardscape displace water. For a cold room, go up a size, or use two smaller heaters at opposite ends for even heat and a backup if one fails.

The dial sets a temperature from roughly 20 to 34 °C, and a red light shows when the heater is actively heating. Set it, wait a day, then check with a separate thermometer such as the [digital thermometer](/product/digital-thermometer-lcd) and adjust. The tank-size pages show the heater wattage that suits each tank, and most tropical community fish are kept at about 24 to 27 °C.

The heater is fully submersible and comes with suction cups. Let it sit in the water for a few minutes before plugging it in and unplug it and let it cool before taking it out. Place it near the filter outlet, where flow spreads the heat.

Thin liquid-crystal strips that stick to the outside of the glass and show the tank temperature in about a minute. They read both Celsius and Fahrenheit in the range 18 to 34 °C, need no batteries and put nothing in the water, so you can put one on every tank.

Stick one to clean, dry glass on the side of the tank away from the heater, below the waterline. The colour band shows the current temperature at a glance. Strips are good for a quick check and a rough match when you refill, but less precise than a digital probe, so use a [digital thermometer](/product/digital-thermometer-lcd) when exact numbers matter.

sections.h: The cheapest insurance in the hobby
sections.body: If the power cuts out, an air pump stops and water can siphon back down the airline into the pump. That is the classic way pumps die and floors get wet. A one-way check valve lets air travel to the tank but stops water going back.

The valve is push-fit on 3 to 5 mm tubing. Trim the end of the tube square, push it firmly on and make sure the arrow points toward the tank. Fit one on each line. It goes between the pump and the stone or filter. Replace it if airflow drops, since a check valve can stick over time.

Use one on every [air pump](/product/dual-outlet-air-pump) line, especially where the pump sits below the water level. A glass [bubble counter with check valve](/product/bubble-counter-check-valve-set) does the same job on a CO2 line.

A palm-sized USB air pump that keeps water oxygenated when you are away from a mains outlet. Use it for bagged fish in transport, a bucket during a power cut or a quarantine tub. It runs from a phone power bank, a laptop or a USB wall adapter.

Keep one in a drawer with a spare air stone, airline and a charged power bank, and you can keep a tank aerated through a power cut. Fish need oxygen more than filtration for several hours. Cut feeding while the filter is off.

Natural pink Himalayan mineral chunks that dissolve slowly. They are used in soft-water shrimp tanks as a source of calcium and trace minerals between water changes, and as an unusual crystal accent for hardscape or paludarium rockwork.

Test GH and conductivity first with [GH and KH strips](/product/gh-kh-test-strips-7in1) or an [EC meter](/product/ph-ec-meter-4in1), because the right mineral level depends on the species. Add a very small piece, wait a day or two and test again. Use sparingly and follow the product's directions, since more is not better in a tank with sensitive shrimp.

Used as a decoration the chunks slowly dissolve and release minerals, so keep them in a place where flow is gentle and replace them over time. Choose the 200 g or 500 g pack according to how much hardscape you need.

sections.h: Hardness is the number most people skip
sections.body: Seven parameters on one strip, with GH and KH leading, plus pH, nitrate, nitrite and chlorine. KH buffers pH stability, so a low KH means pH can swing. GH measures calcium and magnesium, which drive shrimp moulting and plant growth. Checking both becomes a 30-second habit.

In a planted tank on CO2, KH and pH together help you estimate CO2 level. In a shrimp tank, GH tells you whether the water suits the species. If you mix RO water with tap or remineralise it, test the mix before it goes in. For ammonia and a wider panel, use the [8-in-1 strips](/product/test-strips-8-in-1-100-count).
Follow the time on the pack, read in daylight against the chart, and keep the tub tightly closed and dry. A damp strip gives wrong readings. Test the same way each time, and write the numbers down.

sections.h: Bright accents in a dark scape
sections.body: Bags of natural crystal quartz chips, white and translucent, for accent lines in aquascapes, top dressing on potted plants or bright patches against dark sand. Each 100 g resealable bag is enough for accents and highlights, not for a full substrate layer.

Quartz is inert, so it does not swing pH or hardness, and is safe in any freshwater tank. Use it to mark a path or a river line, or to make a bright patch in front of a dark rock. Rinse it first. Wash off dust in a sieve under running water until the water runs clear, then lay it over [aqua soil](/product/aqua-soil-planted-substrate) or sand.

A fired-ceramic cave that gives shy fish and shrimp a dark, defensible shelter. Plecos lay inside it, cichlids claim it and shrimp colonies swarm it after moulting. The aquarium-safe ceramic has a natural matte finish.

Cave-spawning species such as bristlenose, Apistogramma and kribensis need a covered site to spawn. Place the cave on the substrate with the opening facing away from the main swimming area, and give each pair its own cave in a community tank. Leave algae and biofilm on the cave, since the fry graze on it.
Rinse it in clean water before use. Do not move a cave that has eggs in it. A quick swish in old tank water is enough to clear debris, and you can reuse the cave for years.

sections.h: What a UV lamp can and cannot do
sections.body: A submersible UV lamp clarifies green water and knocks back suspended algae, bacteria and parasites in the water column. Algae that float freely pass the lamp and are scrambled, so green fog water clears. It does not touch algae growing on glass, plants or decor.

The 5 W lamp suits tanks up to 200 litres and the 11 W lamp suits tanks up to 500 litres. Run it a few hours a day, or longer for a stubborn bloom, and leave the filter on so that water keeps passing the lamp. Fit it where flow carries water past the light.

UV is harmful to eyes and skin, so never look at the lamp or run it out of the water. Unplug it before handling, and keep it fully submerged when it is on. Check the lamp output over time, since UV tubes lose strength and are usually replaced after some months.

A double-sided printed backdrop that hides wires, walls and reflections. One side shows a deep ocean scene and the other a lush planted scene. Tape it on, flip it if you redecorate, and the tank reads deeper straight away.

Measure the height and length of the back glass, and trim the poster with scissors. Tape it to the outside of the back glass so that no gap lets light in. A dark, busy background makes plants and fish stand out, and a covered back panel reduces reflections. For a deeper 3D effect, see the [3D background](/product/3d-aquarium-background).

A natural driftwood branch gives a tank instant age. Plant anubias or moss on the limbs, let shrimp graze the biofilm and use the branch as a focal point. It is sinkable hardwood that waterlogs within a few days, and boiling or soaking speeds it up.

Boil or soak the branch until it sinks. A small stone tied on top makes it sink right away. Expect tannins to tint the water brown at first. They are harmless and can be removed with [activated carbon](/product/activated-carbon-filter-bags) or by water changes.

Use superglue gel or cotton thread to attach anubias, java fern and moss to the limbs, and keep the roots out of the substrate. Tie them on until they grip. For a full layout, combine with [dragon stone](/product/dragon-stone-ohko-rock) and [aqua soil](/product/aqua-soil-planted-substrate).
